newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices rise in weak volume.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices rise in weak volume.

text.p: Activity faded on Istanbul's gold bourse due to low free market demand on Wednesday while prices rose in line with modest gains recorded in European markets, dealers said.

Traded volume continued to fall sharply to 596 kilos from Tuesday's 727 and Monday's 1,376. Gold closed at 1,099,000 lira per gram and $383.80 an ounce, up from 1,093,000 lira and $383.35 at Tuesday's close.
Dealers said a weak lira also boosted prices in lira terms.

"The active (summer) season is nearing its end, so public demand for gold jewellery and coins is declining. The dollar's recent gains abroad raised gold prices in the domestic market which is another discouraging factor for buyers," said a free market dealer.
Lira deals made up 95 percent of the total trade. 556 kilos of gold changed hands in the first session, followed by only 40 kilos in the afternoon.
Exchange members import gold and prefer to sell it in lira when the daily lira depreciation against the dollar speeds up. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
